findings.claim: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation still indexes DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0] unguarded and casts to PropertyDeclarationSyntax, despite its doc saying it returns null for metadata. For a metadata property on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly (e.g. a member of Item<T> with neither a Key nor an IgnoreMember), it throws IndexOutOfRangeException. The helper only moved the crash, so the reported bug remains for this path. It also can throw InvalidCastException for non-property-declaration syntax such as positional record parameters.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the analyzer/generator on the repro with lib compiled to a metadata reference, where Item<T> has a property with Key(null) or a null string key. Assert no AD0001/CS8785. Alternatively, replace [0] with FirstOrDefault and see whether the test still fails. Also try a positional record struct, whose properties come from a ParameterSyntax.

findings.claim: The reportDiagnostic wrapper silently drops every analyzer diagnostic whose location is not an in-source location in this compilation. Diagnostics created with a null location (e.g. Diagnostic.Create(..., (Location?)null)) have Location.None and are now suppressed. Previously, users' builds could see these for source types. Location.None diagnostics (e.g. from MemberNeedsKey with a null location) or ones located in another syntax tree/partial declarations would no longer be reported, which changes diagnostics and could hide MsgPack errors users relied on.

receipt_plan.detail: Run the existing analyzer tests (MsgPack003/004/005 etc.) plus a case with the type in a partial declaration or a diagnostic with a None location. Check that each expected diagnostic is still reported, comparing results with base and head.
